import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

df = pd.read_excel("/Users/pavithragunasekaran/Documents/sem_3/2026/financial_project/stock_price.xlsx")

#  printing the top 5 rows
print(df.head())
# Converting date column to datetime
df["date"] = pd.to_datetime(df["date"])

# Sort by date 
df = df.sort_values("date")

#  Plot last 1-year stock closing price
plt.figure(figsize=(12, 6))
plt.plot(df["date"], df["close_close_price_adjusted_for_splits"], label="Closing Price")
plt.title("Apple Stock Price - Last 1 Year")
plt.xlabel("Date")
plt.ylabel("Price (USD)")
plt.legend()
plt.grid(True)
plt.show()

# Calculating daily returns
df["Daily Return"] = df["close_close_price_adjusted_for_splits"].pct_change()

#  Measure volatility
volatility = df["Daily Return"].std()
annual_volatility = volatility * (252 ** 0.5)

print("Daily Volatility:", volatility)
print("Annualized Volatility:", annual_volatility)

# Plot daily returns for volatility view
plt.figure(figsize=(12,6))
plt.plot(df['date'], df["Daily Return"])
plt.title("Apple Daily Returns - Last 1 Year")
plt.xlabel("Date")
plt.ylabel("Daily Return")
plt.grid(True)
plt.show()

# Create signal column
df["Signal"] = 0
df.loc[df["20_MA"] > df["50_MA"], "Signal"] = 1
df.loc[df["20_MA"] < df["50_MA"], "Signal"] = -1

# Identify crossover points
df["Trade"] = df["Signal"].diff()

# Buy signal: when 20_MA crosses above 50_MA
buy_signals = df[df["Trade"] == 2]

# Sell signal: when 20_MA crosses below 50_MA
sell_signals = df[df["Trade"] == -2]

# Plotting price, moving averages, and signals
plt.figure(figsize=(12,6))

plt.plot(df["date"], df["close_close_price_adjusted_for_splits"], label="Close Price")
plt.plot(df["date"], df["50_MA"], label="50-Day MA")
plt.plot(df["date"], df["20_MA"], label="20-Day MA")

# Buy markers
plt.scatter(
    buy_signals["date"],
    buy_signals["close_close_price_adjusted_for_splits"],
    label="Buy Signal",
    marker="^",
    s=100
)

# Sell markers
plt.scatter(
    sell_signals["date"],
    sell_signals["close_close_price_adjusted_for_splits"],
    label="Sell Signal",
    marker="v",
    s=100
)
plt.title("Apple - Price Trend with 20,50-day Moving Averages and Trade Signals")
plt.xlabel("Date")
plt.ylabel("Price")
plt.legend()
plt.grid(True)
plt.show()

Key Insights: Clear bullish trend as price stays mostly above both 20-day and 50-day moving averages. 20-day MA remains above 50-day MA for most of the period, confirming sustained upward momentum. Strong price rally after August with both moving averages trending upward smoothly. Slight convergence of MAs towards the end indicates possible consolidation or slowing trend. Buy signals appear when 20-day MA crosses above 50-day MA, indicating start of bullish momentum Sell signals appear when 20-day MA crosses below 50-day MA, indicating potential downward trend Most signals align with price movement, confirming trend following strategy effectiveness Overall more buy signals than sell signals, supporting a strong upward trend in Apple stock

price_col = "adj_close"   
prices = df[price_col].dropna()

# Calculate daily returns
returns = prices.pct_change().dropna()
mu = returns.mean()          # average daily return
sigma = returns.std()        # daily volatility

#  Monte Carlo Simulation: set the no of simulations to 100 
num_simulations = 100
forecast_days = 30

last_price = prices.iloc[-1]

# Storing all simulation results
simulations = np.zeros((forecast_days, num_simulations))

# Run 100 simulations

for i in range(num_simulations):
    simulated_prices = [last_price]

    for j in range(1, forecast_days):
        random_return = np.random.normal(mu, sigma)
        next_price = simulated_prices[-1] * (1 + random_return)
        simulated_prices.append(next_price)

    simulations[:, i] = simulated_prices

# Convert to DataFrame
sim_df = pd.DataFrame(simulations)
sim_df.index = range(1, forecast_days + 1)
print(sim_df.head())

#  Plot simulation paths
plt.figure(figsize=(12, 6))
plt.plot(sim_df)
plt.title("Monte Carlo Simulation: 100 Stock Price Paths for Next 30 Days")
plt.xlabel("Day")
plt.ylabel("Simulated Stock Price")
plt.grid(True)
plt.show()

# Final day forecast statistics
final_day_prices = sim_df.iloc[-1]

mean_forecast = final_day_prices.mean()
min_forecast = final_day_prices.min()
max_forecast = final_day_prices.max()
p5 = np.percentile(final_day_prices, 5)
p95 = np.percentile(final_day_prices, 95)

print("Last Actual Price is:", last_price)
print("Mean Forecast Price after 30 days:", mean_forecast)
print("Minimum Forecast Price is:", min_forecast)
print("Maximum Forecast Price is:", max_forecast)
print("5th Percentile (Risk Lower Range) is:", p5)
print("95th Percentile (Risk Upper Range) is:", p95)

from prophet import Prophet
# Prophet needs: ds (date), y (value)
df_prophet = df.reset_index()[["date", "adj_close"]]  
df_prophet.columns = ["ds", "y"]

# Building the model
model = Prophet()
model.fit(df_prophet)

# Forecast next 30 days
future = model.make_future_dataframe(periods=30)
forecast = model.predict(future)

# Plot forecast
model.plot(forecast)
plt.title("FB Prophet Forecast - Next 30 Days")
plt.xlabel("Date")
plt.ylabel("Price")
plt.show()

forecast[["ds", "yhat", "yhat_lower", "yhat_upper"]].tail(30)

Blue line - actual historical prices Dark line (yhat) -predicted future trend Shaded area - uncertainty range (confidence interval)

Interpretation of Prophet Results Forecast shows overall trend continuation in downward trend Confidence interval widens - uncertainty increases over time Smooth curve - Prophet captures trend, not random fluctuations

Differnce between Fp prophet forecast and Monte carlo simulation Prophet - Trend-based time series model Monte Carlo - Random simulation using historical volatility Output Type Prophet - Single smooth forecast curve Monte Carlo - Multiple simulated price paths Volatility Representation Prophet - Low (smooth, ignores daily randomness) Monte Carlo - High (captures real market fluctuations) Risk Measurement Prophet - Confidence interval (upper & lower bounds) Monte Carlo - Percentile range (5%–95%) Trend Insight Prophet - Clearly shows direction (up/down trend) Monte Carlo - No fixed trend, shows possible scenarios Uncertainty Handling Prophet - Gradual widening of forecast range Monte Carlo - Wide spread depending on volatility Use Case Prophet - Understanding future trend direction Monte Carlo - Understanding risk and variability
